A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeoSplatting and retain the same underlying mesh-to-Gaussian framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial methodological and experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original novel-view synthesis, decomposition, relighting, geometry-recovery and ablation results, including additional experiments in Appendices B, D, E and F.

after.justification: v3 reports original inverse-rendering and normal-estimation results, component ablations, real-world demonstrations, and appendix experiments on shape consistency, refinement, resolution and path tracing.

M1.justification: Although FlexiCubes and the six-Gaussian MGadapter remain, v3 replaces split-sum rendering plus residual color with Monte Carlo rendering, BVH-accelerated mesh occlusion and directional indirect lighting. It introduces deferred-shading refinement and revises attribute modeling and regularization. Appendices H and I additionally implement existing-mesh initialization and path-tracing variants.

E1.justification: Synthetic4Relight and TensoIR are retained; TensoIR already appeared in v1 Appendix F.3. v3 adds the Shiny Blender reflective-object suite, Stanford-ORB objects, Garden outdoor captures and scene-level demonstrations using initial meshes. The full NeRF Synthetic NVS evaluation, DTU experiments and dedicated four-scene geometry-recovery suite from v1 are removed.

E2.justification: Within the retained Synthetic4Relight comparison, v3 adds NVdiffrecmc, TensoIR and NeRO. Within TensoIR, it adds NVdiffrecmc, NeRO and GS-Shader. Appendix I introduces MIRRES as a comparator. The earlier NeuS2 geometry comparison and non-relightable NVS comparisons disappear. GS-Shader and GaussianShader refer to the same retained method.

E3.justification: The reported geometry resolution changes from 96 cubed in v1 to 72 cubed for simple shapes and 96 cubed otherwise in v3. Vertex sampling changes from the first 2% to 5% of training. Geometry evaluation shifts from Chamfer distance/F-score to normal MAE, and new protocols measure reflection-direction and transfer-distance errors, refinement displacement and resolution sensitivity.

E4.justification: v3 replaces the earlier residual-color and second-stage analyses with broader ablations of shape alignment, appearance refinement, occlusion and indirect lighting (Table 3). It adds shape-consistency measurements, refinement-displacement measurements, resolution comparisons and path-tracing analysis. v1's quantitative mask-removal and 2D-versus-3D splatting studies, along with exposure-related failure studies, are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeat counts, seed values, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Dataset averages and Monte Carlo rendering calculations do not constitute newly added uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Results are substantially revised. Synthetic4Relight relighting PSNR/LPIPS are 31.65/0.032 in v1 Table 2 and 34.10/0.037 in v3 Table 1; roughness MSE is respectively 0.017 and 0.004. These accompany method and setting changes, not controlled same-setting gains. v3 adds normal, component-ablation, consistency and path-tracing results while removing earlier benchmark and per-scene entries.

T1.justification: Formal definitions and assumptions change locally: v3 adds the metalness factor to the diffuse BRDF, replaces depth-map-based shape consistency with reflection-direction and transfer-distance criteria, and introduces a monochrome-lighting assumption for regularization. The central MGadapter equations remain. No theorem or proof is added; the referenced error-bound analysis in Appendix B.3 consists of empirical measurements.

C1.justification: The shared geometry-guided Gaussian contribution remains, but v3 makes opaque mesh surfaces and efficient occlusion-aware light transport central contributions in its abstract and introduction. Its conclusion emphasizes normal accuracy, material disentanglement and efficiency relative to implicit-field methods, replacing v1's stronger emphasis on NeRF/DTU results and novel-view synthesis.

C2.justification: v1 identifies shadows baked into albedo and leaves ray tracing to future work. v3 explains how occlusion modeling addresses this problem and discusses the remaining indirect-light approximation and path-tracing cost. It adds explanations of deferred shading, coarse-mask applicability, resolution costs and the failure of initial-mesh reconstruction on specular objects, while dropping detailed lighting-inconsistency and underexposure discussions.

D1.justification: v3 supplies implementation details for revised attribute networks and losses, refinement at learning rate 0.001 for 100 steps, and coarse-mask generation using 5,000 3DGS steps. It adds resolution-dependent GPU-memory and runtime information and identifies ReSTIR for path tracing. A project-page link is added, although both conclusions still describe code release as future work.

R1.justification: v3 adds a rendering-equation-evaluation subsection positioning its approach against split-sum, spherical-Gaussian and Gaussian ray-tracing methods. Appendix B.3 substantively distinguishes MGadapter from MeshSplats and other mesh-Gaussian alignment approaches. References and discussion expand to deferred shading, MIRRES, ReSTIR and additional surface-reconstruction methods.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten around light transport. Methodology gains a dedicated light-transport section, experiments are reorganized around inverse rendering and normal quality, and the appendices are substantially restructured. This exceeds terminology changes or relocation of existing material.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. The teaser, pipeline and MGadapter figures are redesigned, and new occlusion, refinement and normal-comparison illustrations replace much of the earlier gallery. Results are consolidated into a multi-dataset table, with new ablation and appendix tables and different visual highlighting.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's acknowledged shadow-disentanglement deficiency through explicit occlusion modeling and targeted evidence: Table 3 reports relighting PSNR of 27.36 without occlusion versus 29.95 for the full model. Stronger relevant baselines and analyses of alignment, refinement and resource tradeoffs strengthen the central argument. Removed per-scene and failure-case detail, plus unexplained score differences between v3 Tables 1 and 7, limit transparency but do not outweigh these gains.
